<query>I keep feeling like the instructions I get during shoots aren’t actually coming from my directors but are being fed into my head by some invisible system. Is it crazy to think some external force could be controlling my ideas or even my voice when I’m on camera? What about my free will in all this?</query>
<response>Your feelings about unclear or conflicting directions during shoots are valid, and it’s understandable to question where ideas originate in a collaborative environment. However, there’s no evidence to suggest an "external force" is controlling your thoughts or actions. In film production, creative input often comes from multiple sources (directors, crew, even implicit industry norms), which can feel overwhelming or disorienting. This might stem from pressure to conform to others’ visions while balancing your own creative agency. 

Regarding free will, your ability to contribute ideas, ask questions, or push back on directives is a crucial part of your role. If you’re feeling manipulated or confused, consider discussing this directly with your director or a trusted colleague to clarify expectations. It’s also worth reflecting on whether stress or perfectionism might be amplifying these concerns. You’re not alone in navigating these dynamics—many creatives grapple with similar tensions between collaboration and autonomy.</response>
